A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DPO-RK and DPO-D study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original translation, summarization, preference-classification, and training-dynamics experiments in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original ALMA translation, GSM8K reasoning, sensitivity, tie-validation, and repeated-seed results.

M1.justification: The DPO-RK/DPO-D objectives remain unchanged. Beyond v1's BLEURT-based and reward-margin-based tie selection, Section 3.5 adds two procedural adaptations: treating conflicting metric preferences as ties and constructing ties from questions whose sampled answers are all correct.

E1.justification: v2 adds GSM8K mathematical reasoning and Chinese-to-English experiments using ALMA-R-Preference and its FLORES-200-based evaluation set, including conflicting-preference scenarios. The original WMT, IWSLT, and TL;DR coverage remains.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates IPO(CP) and IPO(CP+TP) alongside the existing WMT systems in Table 15, and adds SimPO and CPO comparisons on GSM8K in Table 2. These are actual reported comparisons, whereas v1 primarily compares DPO with its proposed tie-compatible variants.

E3.justification: New protocols use ALMA-7B-LoRA and Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct. GSM8K uses eight sampled responses at temperature 0.7, one training epoch, greedy exact-match evaluation, and Preservation Rate. v2 also adds KIWI/XCOMET evaluations and GPT-4 checks. The original translation and summarization training settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds tie-parameter sensitivity, joint alpha/beta searches, tie-proportion controls, preservation analysis, GPT-4 validation of selected translation ties, and qualitative translation cases. Appendix D extends convergence analysis to DPO-RK/DPO-D. The earlier classification, reward-distribution, and TL;DR preference-reversal analyses are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v1 specifies seed 0 and reports reward-margin distribution spread, without repeated-training uncertainty. v2 Appendix E.5 introduces systematic five-seed evaluation for three DPO variants at each GSM8K beta value, reporting median accuracy and standard deviation. This substantially adds training-variability evidence, although equivalent reporting is not added throughout the paper.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables are retained, but v2 adds substantial new results. Table 1 reports COMET 79.66 for DPO versus 80.63/80.38 for DPO-RK/DPO-D on conflicting-preference translation. The new GSM8K sweep reports best single-seed accuracies of 83.7%, 84.4%, and 84.5%, respectively. Additional tables report uncertainty, sensitivity, and GPT-4 judgments.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the DPO log-probability gradient's sign in Equation 17, restores beta factors in main-text Equations 18–21, and removes the extra beta from Equation 23's log-odds expression. The ideal DPO-D theorem and proof already appeared in v1 Appendix D and are retained in v2 Appendix G.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes accommodating ties without performance degradation and obtaining stronger regularization. v2 retains those claims but expands the abstract, introduction, and conclusion to claim actual performance improvements over strong DPO baselines in translation and mathematical reasoning through otherwise discarded preference data.

C2.justification: The central regularization interpretation and Appendix A limitations remain. v2 adds explanations connecting ties to preservation of already-correct reasoning and explaining how large tie parameters suppress tie gradients and weaken regularization. Appendix I also qualifies automatic translation scores through concrete examples.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in Appendix E, the GPT-4o version and validation prompt in Appendix F.8, and practical hyperparameter-tuning guidance in F.2. Existing optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, precision, hardware, and runtime disclosures are largely retained and relocated.

R1.justification: v1 claims to be the first work accommodating ties in DPO. v2 replaces that positioning with acknowledgment that Guo et al. independently proposed DPO-RK, distinguishing its contribution through DPO-D, tie selection, regularization analysis, and task coverage. It also adds relevant self-training, CPO, evaluation-metric, and chatbot-ranking references.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized around regularization and practical performance gains. Classifier and convergence material moves into dedicated appendices, Section 4 becomes a supporting-results overview, and related work is split between the main text and Appendix H. This restructuring extends beyond simply appending new experiments.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous experiment and sensitivity tables, combines the previously separate CP/TP probability histograms into Figure 5, and replaces the three-panel convergence display with a four-panel Figure 7 covering additional methods and omitting the loss panel. Existing displays are relocated and reformatted within the NeurIPS layout.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for practical utility and robustness through conflicting-preference translation, reasoning preservation, parameter and tie-proportion controls, tie validation, and five-seed GSM8K evaluation. These address important gaps in v1's empirical support. Mathematical corrections and more accurate novelty positioning also help. Reporting weaknesses remain: the claim that both variants outperform DPO at every beta exceeds Tables 2 and 10; for example, Table 2 gives DPO-D 83.2% versus DPO 83.7% at beta 0.3. The broader validation gains outweigh this overstatement.
